questions.explanation: A precise definition prevents the caricature from slipping back in. Testimonial knowledge rests on the reliability of testimony and background evidence. This is the position defended by David Hume. The claim that testimonial knowledge requires no assessment of the speaker's reliability is a common mistake about the view, often described as "credulous misreading of testimony". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: testimony can be mistaken. Noting what the position does and does not claim resolves the matter.
